title: HITS-CLIP/CLIP-Seq/PTB-Seq
scope: Illumina explanatory RNA-contact-capture schematic, with explicitly qualified named applications and the cited Gillen modification. The complete drawing has a descriptive CLIP-Seq/HITS-CLIP title cartoon at left (blue protein, purple RNA, unlabelled yellow accents), then one unbranched main route: RNA-protein complex; UV 254 nm; RNase T1 digestion; Proteinase K; RNA extraction; Reverse transcription; cDNA. Arrows connect the UV and downstream material route; the title cartoon has no transfer arrow and is not a second sample. Green and pink icons are reagent imagery, not retained products. No end groups, compartment labels, molecular identifiers or legend resolve additional chemistry. The graph adds only catalogue-supported antibody selection and broad cDNA-library readout, explicitly marked as text support beyond separate depicted operations. Primer/PCR details of the cited Gillen modification remain version qualifications; listed iCLIP/irCLIP/eCLIP/miCLIP architectures and application-specific library splits are outside the depicted route. No historical development or enzyme-interchangeability edges are inferred.

No cell, bead, compartment, nucleotide end group, barcode or adapter identity is specified in the main input cartoon.

states.label: UV-crosslinked RNA-protein complexes

evidence.quote: This method28,29 uses UV-irradiation to covalently crosslink RNA-protein complexes that are in direct contact (∼single Angstrom distances) within cells, allowing them to be stringently purified. evidence.quote: Here we use HITS-CLIP to covalently crosslink native Argonaute (Ago) protein-RNA complexes in mouse brain. This produced two simultaneous datasets—Ago-miRNA and Ago-mRNA binding sites—that were combined with bioinformatic analysis to identify miRNA-target mRNA interaction sites.

Ule supports the underlying CLIP concept at abstract level; no historical-priority claim is made.

method_scopes.rationale: The catalogue PTB-Seq reference is Xue et al. PTB-targeted CLIP-seq in HeLa cells. The full text supports anti-PTB selection, UV treatment in general, and sequencing DNA PCR amplicons on Illumina GAII. It does not independently specify the exact 254-nm/T1/proteinase-K route of this diagram; the CLIP procedure is delegated to Yeo et al. The combined methods paragraph also covers RIP-PCR, so its random-primed RT is not assigned to the sequencing library. Only the supported selection/readout interfaces are mapped here. The paper separately constructed monomer- and dimer-associated libraries; that application-specific split is outside the diagram scope.

method_scopes.rationale: The card explicitly cites this modification. Shared downstream protein digestion, RNA recovery, RT and cDNA-library readout are supported, while the T1 operation is not assigned to it: Gillen describes RNAse A digestion before immunoprecipitation. Its distinguishing library interface uses a nested RT primer and a reverse PCR primer protected by phosphorothioate bonds at the 3′ end, to suppress amplification of misprimed cDNAs. These unshown primer/PCR details qualify this version and are not added as steps in the figure route or generalized to PTB-Seq.

evidence.locator: Full text, Background [b00013], construction order in the HITS-CLIP implementation discussed by Gillen
evidence.quote: HITS-CLIP library construction [1] begins with the cross-linking of RNA-binding proteins to RNA using UV light, partial RNA digestion with RNAse A, and immunoprecipitation of the RNA-binding protein of interest and attached RNAs.
evidence.rationale: This implementation uses RNAse A before immunoprecipitation. It does not validate universal RNase T1 usage or the catalogue ordering for all HITS-CLIP variants.

evidence.locator: Full text, Background [b00013], protein digestion and RNA recovery
evidence.quote: The resulting size-selected protein-RNA complexes are then digested with Proteinase K to remove the protein and the remaining RNA is purified by phenol extraction and ethanol precipitation.

evidence.locator: Full text, Results [b00021] and Figure 2 explanation, primer-selection modification
evidence.quote: By using a nested reverse transcription primer that lacks the first three bases of the 3′ adaptor, along with a full-length reverse PCR primer with phosphorothioate bonds protecting the final four bases, only cDNAs resulting from priming on 3′ adaptor sequences will be valid templates for PCR amplification.
evidence.rationale: This is the distinguishing primer/PCR interface of the explicitly cited Gillen modification. It is not drawn in the Illumina schematic and is not assigned to the other methods.

evidence.locator: Full text, abstract [b00004], specific Ago implementation
evidence.quote: Here we use HITS-CLIP to covalently crosslink native Argonaute (Ago) protein-RNA complexes in mouse brain. This produced two simultaneous datasets—Ago-miRNA and Ago-mRNA binding sites—that were combined with bioinformatic analysis to identify miRNA-target mRNA interaction sites.
evidence.rationale: This is an Ago-specific implementation, not identification of the generic blue protein in the Illumina image. The two RNA datasets and their computational association do not establish a ligated miRNA-mRNA readout in this schematic.

evidence.locator: Full text, introduction [b00007], UV contact capture and partial digestion
evidence.quote: This method28,29 uses UV-irradiation to covalently crosslink RNA-protein complexes that are in direct contact (∼single Angstrom distances) within cells, allowing them to be stringently purified. Partial RNA digestion reduces bound RNA to fragments that can be sequenced by high throughput methods, yielding genome wide maps and functional insights26,30.

evidence.locator: Full text, Results [b00009], Ago capture and RNA classes
evidence.quote: To purify Ago bound to mouse brain RNAs, we UV-irradiated P13 neocortex and immunoprecipitated Ago under stringent conditions.

evidence.locator: Full text, Methods summary [b00029]
evidence.quote: High-throughput sequencing was performed with an Illumina Genome Analyzer.

evidence.locator: Full text, Introduction [b00009]
evidence.quote: Here we employed CLIP-seq to identify direct RNA targets for PTB in HeLa cells, finding that PTB bound to intronic regions near the 5’ or 3’ splice site regardless of whether the site is subject to regulation.

evidence.quote: In preparation for genome-wide analysis of PTB binding by CLIP-seq, we first characterized a monoclonal anti-PTB antibody (BB7, described in Chou et al., 2000) on HeLa cells before and after UV treatment by immunoprecipitation/Western blotting.

evidence.locator: Full text, Results [b00014], two library populations
evidence.quote: To detect potential functional differences between the monomeric and dimeric forms of PTB, we separately isolated the two protein-RNA complexes and constructed two independent libraries for CLIP-seq analysis.
evidence.rationale: These are paper-specific library populations, outside the single unbranched Illumina route. They are not evidence of a material-pooling branch in the supplied image.

evidence.locator: Full text, Results [b00015], sequenced carrier and platform
evidence.quote: Having thoroughly characterized the libraries, we next subjected PCR amplicons to high-throughput sequencing on the Illumina GAII platform,
evidence.rationale: The physical sequenced carrier in this PTB application is amplified DNA derived from the RNA library; PTB itself is not sequenced.

evidence.locator: Full text, Experimental procedures [b00051]-[b00052], combined CLIP-seq/RIP-PCR/validation subsection
evidence.quote: The CLIP procedure was performed as described (Yeo et al., 2009).
evidence.rationale: The accessible subsection delegates the CLIP procedure and also discusses RIP-PCR validation. Its N9-primed RT/PCR description is not sufficient to assign those primers to the high-throughput sequencing library. Exact RNase identity, the 254-nm wavelength and the depicted protease/RT implementation are not independently specified here.

evidence.rationale: Abstract evidence supports CLIP capture/selection, not the exact RNase T1 chemistry, a complete reaction order, or a historical-priority claim.

corrections.diagram_observation: The image describes CLIP-Seq/HITS-CLIP and depicts an RNA-protein complex, RNase digestion, RNA extraction and cDNA. The catalogue labels Johnson et al. PMID 17540862 as the CLIP-Seq reference.
corrections.primary_statement: The supplied Johnson abstract describes chromatin immunoprecipitation and direct DNA sequencing (ChIPSeq) for protein-DNA interactions. The paper match is therefore background/mismatched citation rather than support for this RNA architecture. The depicted RNA route is retained, with independent CLIP/HITS-CLIP evidence; no DNA branch is inserted.
